desc:
Given an integer array nums (values may be negative) and a positive integer k, return the length of the shortest non-empty contiguous subarray whose sum is divisible by k. If there is no such subarray, return -1.

nums = [3, 1, 4, 2], k = 5
[1, 4] sums to 5, no single element is divisible by 5
result = 2
hints: A block i..j-1 has sum divisible by k when its two prefix sums have the same remainder modulo k.
For a fixed right end, the shortest block uses the most recent earlier prefix with the same remainder. Python's % already returns a non-negative remainder for negative sums.
Keep a dictionary last[remainder] = prefix index, initialised with {0: 0} for the empty prefix. For each new prefix update the answer with j - last[rem] if present, then overwrite last[rem] = j.
editorial: Let P[j] be the sum of the first j elements. The block between prefix positions i < j has sum P[j] - P[i], which is a multiple of k iff P[i] ≡ P[j] (mod k). So the task is: find two prefix positions with equal remainders that are as close together as possible.

For a given j the best partner is the nearest earlier position with the same remainder, so a dictionary storing only the latest index per remainder is enough. Start with remainder 0 at index 0 (the empty prefix, which lets a prefix itself qualify). Overwriting the stored index after each lookup keeps it the latest. The scan is O(n) time and O(min(n, k)) space. Negative sums are handled by taking remainders that are always in [0, k).
